results.title: Symmetric polynomials in the roots are polynomials in the coefficients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A symmetric polynomial is a polynomial in the elementary symmetric polynomials, with a single witness `q` depending only on `f`; consequently, for every monic split polynomial `P`, that same `q` evaluated at the signed coefficients of `P` equals `f` evaluated at the roots of `P`. This is the book's corollary that a symmetric polynomial in the roots of `P` can be written as a polynomial in the coefficients of `P`;…

results.title: Chinese remainder theorem as an algebra isomorphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a commutative semiring, let $R$ be a commutative ring that is a $K$-algebra, and let $(I_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a family of ideals of $R$ indexed by a finite type $\iota$ that are pairwise coprime, that is, $I_i + I_j = R$ for $i \ne j$. Then the map sending the class of $r \in R$ to $(r \bmod I_i)_{i \in \iota}$ is an isomorphism of $K$-algebras from $R / \bigcap_i I_i$ to $\prod_i R / I_i$.

results.title: Distance to a subspace as the norm of the projection residual

results.title: Strict derivative of the squared projection residual

results.title: Strict derivative of the squared distance to a subspace
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Second derivative of the squared norm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real inner product space. For all $p, u, v \in E$, the second Fréchet derivative of $x \mapsto \|x\|^2$ at $p$, applied to $u$ and then to $v$, equals $2 \langle u, v \rangle$.

results.title: A radial primitive is continuously differentiable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let `f` be continuous on `[0, ∞)` with `f 0 = 0`. Then the radial primitive `w ↦ ∫ t in 0..‖w - z₀‖, f t` is continuously differentiable (`C¹`) on the whole real inner product space, including at the centre `z₀`; `f` itself need not be differentiable.

results.title: Fréchet derivative of a radial primitive through its centre
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let `f` be continuous on `[0, ∞)` with `f 0 = 0`. Then `w ↦ ∫ t in 0..‖w - z₀‖, f t` has real Fréchet derivative `(f ‖z - z₀‖ / ‖z - z₀‖) • innerSL ℝ (z - z₀)` at every point `z`, including the centre `z₀`, where this derivative is `0`. The hypothesis `f 0 = 0` is what makes the centre case true.

results.title: Twice the Wirtinger derivative of a sum of radial primitives
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a finite family of profiles `f α`, each continuous on `[0, ∞)` with `f α 0 = 0`, and centres `z₀ α` in `ℂ`, include the real sum `W w = ∑ α ∈ s, ∫ t in 0..‖w - z₀ α‖, f α t` in `ℂ`. Then `2 * barDeriv W z`, which is `∂ₓW + i ∂ᵧW` for the real derivatives, equals `∑ α ∈ s, (f α ‖z - z₀ α‖ / ‖z - z₀ α‖) * (z - z₀ α)` at every `z`. Each summand is `0` at its own centre `z₀ α`; the sum need not vanish there.

results.title: Edge coloring instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of EDGE COLORING is a triple $(n, E, K)$ consisting of a natural number $n$, the number of vertices, a finite list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers, the edges, and a natural number $K$, the bound on the number of colors.

results.title: Adjacency in an edge coloring edge list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers and natural numbers $u$ and $v$, the boolean adjacency of $u$ and $v$ in $E$ is true exactly when $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ occurs in $E$.

results.title: Well-formed edge coloring instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An edge coloring instance $(n, E, K)$ is well formed when the list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(a, b)$ in $E$ satisfies $a < n$, $b < n$ and $a \ne b$, and $(b, a)$ does not occur in $E$.

results.title: Feasible edge coloring instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $(n, E, K)$ be an edge coloring instance with edge list $E = (e_0, \dots, e_{m-1})$, where the endpoints of a pair $(x, y)$ are $x$ and $y$. The instance is feasible when there is a list $(c_0, \dots, c_{m-1})$ of natural numbers with $c_j < K$ for every $j$ such that $c_a \ne c_b$ for all distinct $a, b < m$ for which $e_a$ and $e_b$ share an endpoint.

results.title: EDGE COLORING as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The EDGE COLORING decision problem accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of edge coloring instances, to an instance that is well formed and feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode are rejected.

results.title: EDGE COLORING is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The EDGE COLORING decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.

api: Preorder vertex list of a rooted tree
Preorder vertex list of a node

results.title: Rooted ordered tree
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A rooted ordered tree with vertices in a type $V$ consists of a root vertex in $V$ together with an ordered list of child subtrees, each a rooted ordered tree with vertices in $V$.

results.title: Induction principle for rooted trees
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a property of trees. Suppose that for every vertex $r$ and all trees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ (with $k \ge 0$), if $P$ holds for each $c_i$, then $P$ holds for the tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$. Then $P$ holds for every tree.

results.title: Root of a rooted tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The root of the tree with root vertex $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ is the vertex $r$.

results.title: Children of a rooted tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The children of a tree are the child subtrees of its root, as a list in their given order.

results.title: Size of a rooted tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The size of a tree is its number of nodes, counting repeated vertex labels with multiplicity: the tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ has size $1 + \sum_{i=1}^{k} \operatorname{size}(c_i)$.

results.title: Accumulator preorder traversal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a rooted ordered tree $t$ with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ (in order) and a list $a$, the accumulator traversal $T(t, a)$ is the list whose first entry is $r$ and whose remaining entries are $T(c_1, T(c_2, \dots, T(c_k, a) \dots))$; when $k = 0$ the remaining entries are $a$.

results.title: Preorder vertex list of a rooted tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The preorder vertex list of a rooted ordered tree $t$ is the accumulator preorder traversal of $t$ started from the empty list.

results.title: Accumulator preorder traversal is append
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every rooted ordered tree $t$ and every list $a$, the accumulator preorder traversal of $t$ started from $a$ equals the preorder vertex list of $t$ followed by $a$.

results.title: Preorder vertex list of a node
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a vertex $r$ and rooted ordered trees $c_1, \dots, c_k$, the preorder vertex list of the tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ (in order) is $r$ followed by the concatenation of the preorder vertex lists of $c_1, \dots, c_k$, in this order.

results.title: Euler tour with an accumulator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $t$ be a tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ in order, and let $a$ be a list of vertices. For a list $L$ of vertices, write $r \cdot L$ for the list $L$ with $r$ put in front. The Euler tour of $t$ with accumulator $a$, written $T(t, a)$, is $r \cdot L_1$, where $L_{k+1} = a$ and $L_i = T(c_i, r \cdot L_{i+1})$ for $i = k, \dots, 1$.

results.title: Euler tour
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Euler tour of a tree $t$ with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ in order is the list of vertices consisting of $r$, followed, for each $i = 1, \dots, k$ in turn, by the Euler tour of $c_i$ and then $r$. It is the vertex sequence of the depth-first walk that returns to the parent vertex after each child subtree.

results.title: Accumulator lemma for the Euler tour
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every tree $t$ and every list $a$ of vertices, the Euler tour of $t$ with accumulator $a$ equals the Euler tour of $t$ followed by $a$.

results.title: Recursive formula for the Euler tour
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a vertex $r$ and a list of trees $c_1, \dots, c_k$, the Euler tour of the tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$ in order is $r$, followed, for each $i = 1, \dots, k$ in turn, by the Euler tour of $c_i$ and then $r$.

results.title: Arc sequence of the Euler tour
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The arc sequence of a tree $t$ is the list of consecutive pairs of its Euler tour: if the Euler tour of $t$ is $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_k$, then the arc sequence of $t$ is $(v_0, v_1), (v_1, v_2), \dots, (v_{k-1}, v_k)$.

results.title: Arc sequence as the zipped Euler tour
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every tree $t$, the arc sequence of $t$ is the Euler tour of $t$ zipped with its own tail: if the Euler tour of $t$ is $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_k$, then the arc sequence of $t$ is $(v_0, v_1), (v_1, v_2), \dots, (v_{k-1}, v_k)$.

results.title: The Euler tour visits exactly the vertices of the tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every tree $t$ and every $v$, $v$ occurs in the Euler tour of $t$ if and only if $v$ is a vertex of $t$.

results.title: Valid Euler-tour tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A rooted ordered tree is valid when its list of vertices in preorder has no duplicates, that is, every vertex label occurs at most once in the tree.

results.title: Valid trees have distinct vertices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A tree $t$ is valid if and only if its list of vertices in preorder has no repeated entries.

results.title: A single-vertex tree is valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every vertex $r$, the tree with root $r$ and no child subtrees is valid.

results.title: Linking two rooted trees
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $t_1$ be a tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$, and let $t_2$ be a tree. The link of $t_1$ and $t_2$ is the tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k, t_2$, so $t_2$ becomes the new last child subtree of the root of $t_1$.

results.title: Linking valid trees with disjoint vertices gives a valid tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t_1$ and $t_2$ be valid trees such that no vertex of $t_1$ is a vertex of $t_2$. Then the link of $t_1$ and $t_2$, that is, $t_1$ with $t_2$ added as the last child subtree of its root, is valid.

results.title: Linking two copies of a single vertex is not valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every vertex $r$, the link of the single-vertex tree with root $r$ and another single-vertex tree with root $r$ is not valid, since the vertex $r$ occurs twice in it. Hence the link of two valid trees need not be valid when their vertex sets are not disjoint.

results.title: Splicing two Euler tours
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For lists $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ of vertices and a vertex $r$, the splice of $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ at $r$ is the list consisting of the entries of $\tau_1$, followed by the entries of $\tau_2$, followed by $r$.

results.title: Euler tour of a linked tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For trees $t_1$ and $t_2$, let $t$ be the link of $t_1$ and $t_2$, that is, $t_1$ with $t_2$ added as the last child subtree of its root. The Euler tour of $t$ is the Euler tour of $t_1$, followed by the Euler tour of $t_2$, followed by the root of $t_1$.

results.title: Cutting the last child subtree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $t$ be a tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_k$. Cutting the last child subtree of $t$ gives no result when $k = 0$; when $k \ge 1$ it gives the pair consisting of the tree with root $r$ and child subtrees $c_1, \dots, c_{k-1}$, together with the removed subtree $c_k$.
